prompt.context: Your client is an Italian television broadcasting company. It has rights for broadcasting the Champions League Soccer Tournament in Italy. We have been asked to decide whether to broadcast it on a pay-TV channel owned by the client or on the free channel also owned by the client.
prompt.question: What should our client do — broadcast the Champions League on its pay-TV channel or on its free channel?

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue sources for each option?
clarifying_info.a: Free TV generates ad revenue; pay TV generates additional subscribers.

clarifying_info.q: What is the ad rate for free TV?
clarifying_info.a: 30 seconds of ads cost $70K at any stage; games have 25 minutes of advertising.

First round: 4 groups of 4 teams each; each team plays every other team in its group on a neutral field; top 2 advance. Second round: quarterfinals with home and away games. Third round: semifinals (home and away), then the final.

clarifying_info.q: Which games does our client broadcast?
clarifying_info.a: The client broadcasts only games with at least one Italian team. There are 3 Italian teams, each in a different group. Assume all Italian teams advance through every round.

clarifying_info.q: What is the opportunity cost if we don't broadcast on free TV?
clarifying_info.a: If we decide not to broadcast on free TV, we still get the same ad minutes at $20K per minute.

clarifying_info.q: What are the pay-TV subscriber numbers?
clarifying_info.a: Broadcasting on pay TV will bring in 1 million new subscribers for the year.

Subscription fee (sign-up) is $10; monthly price is $5. Customer acquisition cost is $5 per new subscriber; annual cost to serve each account is $6. No existing customers will leave if we do not broadcast on pay TV. The project lasts only 1 year.

framework: Determine the number of games the client will broadcast (based on tournament structure and Italian team assumption)
Calculate incremental revenue for the free-TV scenario (ad revenue minus opportunity cost of foregone alternative programming)
Calculate incremental revenue and costs for the pay-TV scenario (new subscriber revenue minus acquisition and service costs)
Compare net incremental profit of both scenarios
Identify qualitative factors and risks that could affect the decision

questions.prompt: How many games will the client broadcast in total?
questions.guidance: Work through each round methodically. First round: each Italian team plays the other 3 teams in its group = 3 games per team × 3 teams = 9 games. Second round (quarterfinals): each Italian team plays a home game and an away game = 2 games × 3 teams = 6 games. Third round (semifinals): same structure = 2 games × 2 remaining Italian teams = 4 games. Final: 1 game. Total = 9 + 6 + 4 + 1 = 20 games.

math.setup: Count broadcasted games per round assuming all 3 Italian teams advance; each team plays all others in group (3 games each) in round 1; home+away in QF and SF; 1 final.
steps: Round 1: 3 Italian teams × 3 games each = 9 games
Round 3 (SF): 2 Italian teams remaining × 2 games = 4 games

questions.prompt: What is the incremental profit for the free-TV scenario?
questions.guidance: Ad revenue per game = 25 minutes × 2 slots per minute × $70K = $3.5M. However, opportunity cost: without the game the client earns $20K/min for the same 25 minutes = $500K. Incremental revenue per game = $3.5M - $500K = $3.0M. Total = 20 × $3.0M = $60M. No additional costs for free TV, so incremental profit = $60M.

math.setup: Incremental ad revenue per game = 25 min × (2 × $70K/30s converted to per-minute rate minus $20K opportunity cost per minute). Note: 30-second slot = $70K, so 1 minute = 2 slots = $140K. Opportunity cost = $20K/min.
steps: Revenue per minute of game broadcast = 2 × $70K = $140K

questions.prompt: What is the incremental profit for the pay-TV scenario?
questions.guidance: 1M new subscribers each pay $10 sign-up + $5/month × 12 months = $70 per subscriber. Total revenue = 1M × $70 = $70M. Costs: acquisition $5 + annual service $6 = $11 per subscriber. Total costs = 1M × $11 = $11M. Incremental profit = $70M - $11M = $59M.

math.setup: Revenue per new subscriber = sign-up fee + monthly fee × 12 months. Cost per new subscriber = acquisition cost + annual service cost.

questions.prompt: Which option should the client choose, and are there additional factors to consider?
questions.guidance: Free TV ($60M) marginally outperforms pay TV ($59M). A strong candidate drives to this conclusion clearly, but a superior answer also raises qualitative considerations: pay-TV subscribers may renew next year (recurring value beyond year 1); pay TV grows subscriber base for future content deals; free TV maximizes viewership and ad inventory; the $1M profit difference is small relative to uncertainty in subscriber assumptions.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the base math, what additional factors or risks might influence whether the client chooses free TV or pay TV?

categories.name: Pay-TV upside
ideas: Subscribers acquired may renew in subsequent years, generating recurring revenue
Growing pay-TV base strengthens negotiating leverage for future content rights
Cross-selling opportunities for other pay-TV content to new subscribers

categories.name: Free-TV upside
ideas: Broader audience reach increases advertiser willingness to pay premium CPM
Brand equity and public profile from mass viewership
Potential to upsell viewers to pay TV after exposure

categories.name: Assumption sensitivity
ideas: Subscriber acquisition estimate (1M) may be optimistic or pessimistic
Churn post-season could erode pay-TV subscriber base before year-end
Ad rates may vary by game importance (group stage vs. final)
Italian team performance: if they exit early, fewer games and lower revenue

categories.name: Strategic considerations
ideas: Regulatory or contractual constraints on pay-TV exclusivity
Competitive response: rival broadcasters adjusting pricing if client moves to pay TV
Long-term rights renewal negotiations influenced by viewership data

recommendation: Broadcast on free TV, which yields $60M in incremental profit vs. $59M for pay TV
The $1M advantage is modest, but free TV also carries no subscriber acquisition risk
risks: The pay-TV subscriber estimate of 1M is the key swing assumption; if actual uptake is higher, pay TV could be superior
Italian team performance is assumed perfect; early exits would reduce the number of games and cut revenue in both scenarios
Opportunity cost rate ($20K/min) could vary if alternative programming demand shifts
next_steps: Validate the 1M new subscriber assumption with historical data from comparable sports rights launches
Model sensitivity of pay-TV NPV over a 2-3 year horizon to capture subscriber renewal value
Assess advertiser demand elasticity to confirm the $140K/min ad rate holds across all 20 games
